title: Coherent uniqueness of contravariant transport along an edge
statement: Use quasicategories, coherent functors and natural equivalences as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and cartesian fibrations as in [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Let $p:E\to B$ be a cartesian fibration of quasicategories, let $f:b\to b'$ be an edge of $B$, and put $E_b=E\times_B\{b\}$ and $E_{b'}=E\times_B\{b'\}$. Suppose $R_0,R_1:E_{b'}\to E_b$ have coherent witnesses $h_j:\Delta^1\times E_{b'}\to E$ satisfying $p h_j=f\operatorname{pr}_{\Delta^1}$, with endpoints $i_b\circ R_j$ at $0$ and $i_{b'}$ at $1$, where $i_b:E_b\hookrightarrow E$ and $i_{b'}:E_{b'}\hookrightarrow E$ are the fiber inclusions, and with $p$-cartesian edges at every vertex. Then $R_0$ and $R_1$ are equivalent objects in $\operatorname{Fun}(E_{b'},E_b)$. In particular, there are coherent transformations $s:R_0\to R_1$ and $t:R_1\to R_0$ with inverse homotopies $ts\simeq1_{R_0}$ and $st\simeq1_{R_1}$ in this functor quasicategory. No cocartesian structure or adjunction is assumed.

source.place: Kerodon 019X, Proposition 5.2.2.17, uniqueness clause; Definition 5.2.2.15 (01VN). Read in full subsection 019M at https://kerodon.net/tag/019M on 2026-10-17 because the individual tag page timed out. Not archived. Kerodon identifiers, not Stacks tags.

proof.text: Choose one universe containing $E,B$ and their fibers, and put $K=E_{b'}$. The fiber $E_b$ is a quasicategory: apply the inner-horn lifting property of $p$ over the constant simplex at $b$. Let $T$ consist of all $p$-cartesian edges of $E$. It contains all degenerate edges: a degenerate edge has itself as inverse with degenerate inverse triangles, so [lem-cbc-inner-fibration-equivalence-outer-horn-lift] fills every final outer horn with this final edge, which is exactly the cartesian criterion. Thus $E^T=(E,T)$ is a marked simplicial set. Use the coordinatewise product markings of [lem-coef-marked-endpoint-prism-generation], and put $U=(\Delta^1)^\sharp\times K^\flat$, with base map $f\operatorname{pr}_{\Delta^1}$, and $A=\{1\}^\sharp\times K^\flat$. The only marked edges of $U$ have constant $K$-coordinate at a vertex; hence the given $h_j$ are marked maps $U\to E^T$ over $B$, both restricting to $a=i_{b'}$ on $A$.

source.place: Proposition 4.4.2.13 for degenerate cartesian edges; the marked witness construction uses the explicit markings in HTT Proposition 3.1.1.5.

proof.text: The marked map $E^T\to B^\sharp$ lifts all the generators $I\cup F$ of [lem-coef-marked-endpoint-prism-generation]. An $I$-problem is an inner-horn problem for $p$, and has no nondegenerate marked edges to check. For $F$ in dimension $n=1$, the problem prescribes a target and a base edge, so the cartesian-fibration hypothesis gives a marked lift. For $F$ in dimension $n\geq2$, its final edge already lies in the horn and is sent to a $p$-cartesian edge, so its filler is precisely the final-horn condition of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]; the only nondegenerate edge required to be marked was already specified. The right lifting property persists under the closure operations defining $\langle I\cup F\rangle$: for a pushout restrict the problem to the attached domain and glue its filler; for a transfinite composite choose fillers successively, taking the compatible colimit map at each limit ordinal; for a retract compose a filler with the two retraction maps. Hence $E^T\to B^\sharp$ lifts every member of $\langle I\cup F\rangle$.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.1.5, classes (1) and (2); direct horn lifting and the elementary closure of a right lifting property.

proof.text:
Define a simplicial set $W$ by taking its $n$-simplices to be marked maps
$$(\Delta^1)^\sharp\times(K\times\Delta^n)^\flat\longrightarrow E^T$$
over the fixed base $f\operatorname{pr}_{\Delta^1}$ whose restriction at interval endpoint $1$ is $i_{b'}\operatorname{pr}_K$. Operators restrict the $\Delta^n$ parameter. Its vertices include $h_0,h_1$. For a prescribed boundary $\partial\Delta^n\to W$, its compatible faces and the fixed terminal diagram give a marked map on
$$((\Delta^1)^\sharp\times(K\times\partial\Delta^n)^\flat)\amalg_{\{1\}^\sharp\times(K\times\partial\Delta^n)^\flat}(\{1\}^\sharp\times(K\times\Delta^n)^\flat).$$
The inclusion of this domain into $(\Delta^1)^\sharp\times(K\times\Delta^n)^\flat$ is $P(K\times\partial\Delta^n\hookrightarrow K\times\Delta^n)$, so [lem-coef-marked-endpoint-prism-generation] places it in $\langle I\cup F\rangle$. Step 2 supplies its marked filler over the same base. This extends the boundary to an $n$-simplex of $W$, including $n=0$. Thus $W\to\Delta^0$ is a trivial Kan fibration in the boundary-lifting sense of [def-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-fibration]. No relative marked model structure or mapping-space theorem is used.

source.place: Proposition 3.1.1.5, class (2-double-prime), applied to K times a boundary inclusion; Stacks 08NL, label definition-trivial-kan, for the resulting lifting terminology.

proof.text: Apply boundary lifting for $W\to\Delta^0$ in dimension one twice, to the ordered endpoint pairs $(h_0,h_1)$ and $(h_1,h_0)$, obtaining edges $\gamma:h_0\to h_1$ and $\delta:h_1\to h_0$. Next prescribe a full two-simplex boundary whose vertices are $(h_0,h_1,h_0)$, whose successive edges are $(\gamma,\delta)$, and whose long edge is the degenerate edge of $h_0$. The vertices match, so this is a well-defined boundary map and lifts in dimension two. Repeat with vertices $(h_1,h_0,h_1)$, successive edges $(\delta,\gamma)$ and the degenerate long edge of $h_1$. The two resulting $2$-simplices supply both inverse triangles in $W$, always with the terminal diagram fixed.

source.place: Stacks Tag 08NL, label definition-trivial-kan, in dimensions one and two.

proof.text:
Restriction to interval endpoint $0$ defines a simplicial map
$$\operatorname{ev}_0:W\longrightarrow\operatorname{Fun}(K,E_b).$$
Indeed an $n$-simplex of $W$ restricts to a map $K\times\Delta^n\to E$ with constant base $b$, which uniquely factors through the degreewise fiber $E_b$. The factorization commutes with all parameter operators. Both $K$ and the parameter have minimal marking, so no edge of $K$ is being required to be cartesian. The vertices $h_j$ map to $R_j$. Let $s=\operatorname{ev}_0(\gamma)$ and $t=\operatorname{ev}_0(\delta)$. The two triangles in step 4 restrict to triangles with successive edges $(s,t)$ and $(t,s)$ and degenerate long edges $1_{R_0}$ and $1_{R_1}$. These are simplices of the full internal functor object, rather than just objectwise comparisons.

source.place: Lecture II, printed p.14, definition of the internal mapping simplicial set; explicit degreewise evaluation.

proof.text: By [lem-cbc-internal-hom-quasicategory], $\operatorname{Fun}(K,E_b)$ is a quasicategory, since $E_b$ is a quasicategory by step 1. By the equivalence-edge definition of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], the edge $s$ with inverse $t$ and these two triangles is an equivalence in that functor quasicategory. Edges there are coherent transformations, and the triangles are exactly $ts\simeq1_{R_0}$ and $st\simeq1_{R_1}$. This proves every clause with $K=E_{b'}$. The construction used only cartesian lifts and the specified coherent witnesses.
